title: serving-runtime-daily-scratchpad-2026-03-21
content:
Daily scratchpad - serving runtime (fast notes, todo, triage)
Date: 2026-03-21
Owner: Evan Brooks

Top priorities:
- triage SRV-4821 (beam search blowup on long sequences) -- blocking canary for T1 customers
- perf experiment: dynamic batching heuristics + kernel A/B (faster attention)
- follow up with infra on dedicated pool eviction behavior for KV cache (SRV-4834)

Morning triage notes:
- SRV-4821: reproduces locally with --seq-len 4096, p95 tokens/second drops 3x after step ~1200. Repro steps saved in /tmp/srv4821-repro-2026-03-21.log. Suspect: KV cache eviction path + stale shard map on fallback.
  - temp workaround: cap sequence length at 2048 in rollout config (canary).
  - next: add extra logging around cache evict and shard remap (L73 in kv_cache.cc).
  - linked: PR 1876 touched eviction timing; ask @Sofia for context.

Perf TODOs / experiments:
- experiment A: batch_size adaptive (based on p95 latency target 120ms)
  - bench command: ./bench --model redwood-7b --mode streaming --target_p95=120 --adaptive-batch=true --runs 50
  - metric to capture: tokens/sec, p50, p95, cost-per-token estimate
  - hypothesis: adaptive batching reduces cost by ~20% with <10% latency regress for avg requests

- experiment B: kernel selection heuristic tweak (current: choose kernel by avg seq length; try stdev-aware selection)
  - change: if seq_len_stdev > 0.6 use kernel-B (better tail behaviour)
  - quick note: kernel-B uses fused-attention2 (see confluence page), slightly higher memory but better tail p95

Kernel notes:
- kernel-A (fused-attn-v1): best for stable short seqs (<512), lower memory, consistent latency
- kernel-B (fused-attn-v2): better long-seq scaling, slightly higher startup cost. Observed 8% better p95 for seq>1024 in last run (2026-03-17)
- TODO: add unit test that simulates mixed-length batch and asserts selection path runs without OOM

KV cache / eviction:
- observed double-free race in kv_cache when remapping shards during concurrent evict+append (rare, low repro rate)
  - suspect race in shard->owner update (kv_cache/shard_map.cc L210)
  - mitigation: add per-shard mutex and CAS on owner field (cheap for common case?)
  - test: fuzz with concurrent append+evict for 10k steps (use local harness in tools/cache_fuzz)

Incidents / customer impact:
- small set of T1 customers saw timeouts when seq len > 2k and throughput high. Set canary cap to 2048 for them for now. Need ops page documenting this fallback.

Notes to self (quick):
- ping @Liam about rolling back PR 1849 (quantization change) if perf regress confirmed
- add trace id to eviction logs for easier cross-service correlation
- review telemetry for last 7 days: focus on p95 by model and by route (console: per-route p95 chart)

Meeting prep for 2pm sync with Sofia / infra:
- share repro for SRV-4821 (link + howto)
- propose short-term canary (cap seq len) + logging change + longer-term fix (mutex/CAS)
- request infra to run dedicated-pool eviction sim on staging cluster (attach job spec)

Questions / unresolved:
- Is there an existing backoff policy for shard remap storms? (searching Confluence didn't show a dedicated doc)
- Will per-shard mutex add unacceptable contention under extremely high throughput? Need microbench.

Quick checklist:
- [ ] add eviction logs with trace_id (low risk)
- [ ] add per-shard mutex prototype + bench script (medium risk)
- [ ] run adaptive-batch bench on g4dn (50 runs) and collect metrics (low risk)
- [ ] update canary config for T1 customers (ops ticket)
- [ ] follow up with Sofia on PR1876 details

Snippets / commands to run locally:
- reproduce SRV-4821:
  ./run_local_repro --model redwood-7b --seq-len 4096 --steps 2000 --out /tmp/srv4821-repro.log
- bench adaptive batching:
  ./bench --model redwood-7b --mode streaming --adaptive-batch=true --target_p95=120 --runs 50 --out results/ab_2026-03-21.json
- fuzz kv cache:
  tools/cache_fuzz --concurrency 8 --iterations 10000 --log /tmp/cache_fuzz.log

References:
- PR 1876 (eviction timing tweak) - https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1876
- Jira SRV-4821 (beam search blowup)
- Confluence: serving-runtime/kernel-selection

Random notes / ideas:
- consider a lightweight eviction telemetry event (counts + latency + owner) to make triage faster
- experiment with pre-allocation of KV slabs for long-seq canaries to avoid dynamic alloc spikes

End of scratchpad.
